key_insight: A lightweight attention-based CNN classified skin lesion images with 87% accuracy, matching MobileNet while using approximately half its parameters and storage.
clinical_relevance: This skin lesion classification study—not drug discovery research—may inform computationally efficient diagnostic support, but does not establish clinical benefit.
method: Used channel attention in a CNN for binary skin lesion classification.
Applied balanced class weights and compared performance with four baseline CNNs.
Generated saliency maps to visualize image regions influencing predictions.
evidence_signal: On a public dataset with 2,637 training and 660 test images, the 1.95-million-parameter model achieved 87% accuracy, ROC AUC 0.9475, and PR AUC 0.9430.
watch_item: External clinical validation is not reported in the abstract, and saliency maps alone do not establish reliable explanations.
paper_title: A Lightweight Attention-Based CNN with Saliency-Map Interpretability for Skin Cancer Detection
